conviction_note: Q3 is mostly locked in, with about 88% of 2026 days fixed per the Q2 call. The below-the-line items offset each other: a Genco mark-to-market gain plus the Genco dividend, about +$14m, against a likely loss on Diana's own warrants and possible write-offs of deal costs. Upside in the window is likely capped by warrant-exercise arbitrage above about $2.38. Findings sum to +0.1 and the scaled number is about 0 on a rebuilt reaction scale of about 4.5%, so this is close to a non-result.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS consensus $0.10 (Q4 2026E $0.21), from a single source: a Benzinga earnings-forecast page updated Oct 27, seen only as a search snippet; the page itself returned 403 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DSX/earnings-forecasts). Earnings Whispers shows no estimate (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/DSX). No revenue consensus was found and the company gives no guidance. The bar is effectively unsourced (one source, unverified), so every finding is capped small. My own Q3 build: revenue about $59-62m (Q2 was $57.3m, TCE $16,581). Below the line: Genco equity-securities gain about +$9.4m and Genco dividend about +$5.0m, against a warrant-liability loss of roughly -$5 to -10m. That gives EPS of about $0.10-0.17, with a point estimate near $0.11-0.12.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,596,373 shares at the Oct 15, 2026 settlement, days to cover 4.42 (Equibles, from FINRA: https://equibles.com/stocks/dsx/short-interest). That is about 3.4% of the 136.9m shares outstanding, so not crowded. Fintel and Benzinga give lower figures. Borrow fee about 1% (curvedtrading). No usable option chain: ATM legs not two-sided, skew null, put/call OI 0.13 (call-heavy, likely left over from the September run to $3.11). Insiders: the Paliou family controls 20.35% (13D/A filed Oct 16, 2026) and exercised 3.53m warrants on Sep 11. Director Palios exercised 376,216 warrants on Nov 10 at an effective $2.36 per share. Run-up 5d +2.0%, 20d -7.4%, and the stock is 25% below its Sep 18 high of $3.11.

findings.finding: Q3 brings a below-the-line gain of about +$14m (about $0.11 per share) from the Genco stake, against a $0.10 EPS bar. Diana held 6,264,548 GNK shares at June 30, carried at $155.2m (= $24.78 each). It sold about 2.13m between Aug 21 and Sep 1 at about $26.1-26.8, booking about +$3.7m over the June mark. The remaining ~4.13m were marked at $26.16 on Sep 30, about +$5.7m. It also received Genco's $0.80 Q2 dividend (record Aug 17) on 6.26m shares, about +$5.0m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 had a $26.4m unrealized Genco gain; EPS 'surprised to the upside' and the stock fell 2.0% (May 27 close 2.52 to May 28 close 2.47). Q2 2026 had a $14.3m equity-securities gain; Jul 29 close 2.14 to Jul 30 close 2.30, +7.5%, on a day that also carried Genco-deal news. So this line has not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: GNK prices are public, so the gain can be worked out mechanically. But only one stale consensus figure ($0.10) exists, and it may or may not include a remeasurement. If the market had fully priced this, the bar would sit nearer $0.15-0.20 rather than below Q2's $0.16.
findings.independence: Sales and prices from GNK Form 4s summarised at https://massive.com/quote/gnk/insider-trading and https://gcaptain.com/diana-shipping-cuts-genco-stake-below-10-weeks-after-abandoning-takeover-bid/ (2026-09-04). GNK closes June 30 $24.78 and Sep 30 $26.16 from Yahoo chart. Genco dividend record date Aug 17 from https://finviz.com/news/378069/genco-shipping-trading-limited-announces-q2-2026-financial-results. The accounting is fair value through P&L, per the Q1 call 'unrealized gain on our investment in Genco of $26.4' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/diana-shipping-dsx-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). All of these document the same stake, so this counts once.

findings.finding: Q3 likely carries a fair-value loss on Diana's own DSX warrants that offsets part of the Genco gain. In Q3, DSX rose from $2.10 (June 30) to $2.75 (Sep 30). Each warrant buys 1.69527 shares for $4.00, a breakeven of about $2.36, so the warrants went from out of the money to about $0.66 of intrinsic value each. Warrants outstanding were about 15.69m at May 27, and about 7m were exercised in September. The estimated 'loss on warrants' is roughly -$5m to -$10m, about -$0.04 to -0.08 per share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 'Gain/(loss) on warrants' line was -$2.2m in Q1 2026, when DSX rose, and +$1.1m in Q2 2026, when DSX fell. The stock's reaction has never been attributed to this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is a single estimate and an analyst would not normally model a liability remeasurement on expiring warrants. If it were in the bar, the $0.10 Q3 estimate would sit visibly below a Q3 that already carries about $0.11 of Genco gains. Caveat, and the reason the size is small: no filing I read confirms the warrants are liability-classified. This is inferred from the line's sign tracking DSX's price.
findings.independence: Warrant terms (1.69527 shares per warrant, $4.00 exercise) come from director Palios's Form 4, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318885/000091957426007547/ownership.xml (2026-11-12). The Q2 line (+$1,147k) is from the Q2 release at https://finviz.com/news/375049/. Both are separate from the finding-1 documents.

findings.finding: Operating Q3 likely improved on Q2's TCE of $16,581. On the Q1 call (May 28) management said 83% of the rest-of-2026 days were fixed at an average of about $18,000/day. On the Q2 call only 12% remained open, with new period cover 'significantly higher than previous charters'. September re-fixtures confirm the step-up: Astarte from $12,500 to $17,000 and DSI Polaris from $12,250 to $18,000. G.P. Zafirakis is fixed at $38,000 from October. The peer read is strong: Genco's Q3 TCE was $27,539 (+73% y/y) and the Capesize 5TC was about $42.8k in mid-November.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed releases: Q3'25 (Nov 20, 2025) -4.5%, Q4'25 (Feb 26, 2026) +4.4%, Q1'26 (May 28) -2.0%, Q2'26 (Jul 30) +7.5%. Q2's TCE +7% y/y coincided with the +7.5% day, though Genco-deal news shared that day.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Every charter is press-released individually and the coverage was stated on two calls. What could still surprise is the Q4/2027 coverage update on the call, against a stock that has fallen 25% since Sep 18 while Capesize rates rose. If the market were extrapolating the re-fixtures, DSX would not be sitting at its July level.
findings.independence: Re-fixtures in the 6-Ks at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318885/000091957426006347/p15082423_exh99-1.htm (2026-09-16) and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318885/000091957426006415/p15096900_exh99-1.htm (2026-09-21). Peer TCE at https://finviz.com/news/416015/genco-shipping-trading-limited-announces-q3-2026-financial-results (2026-11-04). This is a different source from the calls.

findings.finding: Insiders put cash into the company in Q3/Q4 at prices near the current spot, and the share count rose about 10%. Shares outstanding went from 124.41m (Jul 29) to 136.87m (Oct 16) through warrant exercises, implying roughly $29m of cash at $4.00 per warrant. The Paliou family exercised 3,527,501 warrants on Sep 11 (about $14.1m) and now owns 20.35%. Director Palios exercised 376,216 on Nov 10 at an effective $2.36 per share, about spot. The money pays for two methanol dual-fuel Kamsarmax newbuilds (2H27/1H28) and the balance sheet after the Genco bid.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The dilution is visible in the share count. What is not aggregated is that the controlling family and a director paid cash at about the market price two weeks before the print. The financing question has an answer: this is equity paid in by insiders, not distress. The positive is small because the dilution weighs on EPS and NAV per share.
findings.independence: Director Form 4 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318885/000091957426007547/ownership.xml (2026-11-12). Share count in the Q2 release (124,413,717 at Jul 29). Separate filings.

findings.finding: Warrant-exercise arbitrage likely caps a positive reaction in the window. About 8m DSX warrants remain, expiring Dec 14, 2026, at 1.69527 shares per $4.00 warrant. With the warrant at $0.04, breakeven is about $2.38, only 2-3% above the $2.325 seal. Any print-driven move above it lets holders short or sell stock and exercise. That is up to about 13.6m shares, about 19 days of the 711k average daily volume. September showed this: DSX hit $3.11 on Sep 18 while about 7m warrants were exercised, then fell back.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on a print. Shares outstanding rose 12.5m between Jul 29 and Oct 16 while DSX traded above about $2.40, and the stock fell from $3.11 to $2.36.
findings.why_not_priced: The breakeven depends on a bonus-share fraction that has been adjusted for dividends; aggregators quote the $4.00 strike, not the $2.36 effective price. If the market were fully pricing upside supply, the warrant would not trade as low as $0.04 while 13.6m potential shares sit about 3% above spot. This mainly asymmetrises the reaction (downside open, upside capped), so the signed effect is small and negative. Caveat: the company can end the bonus period, which would remove the cap.
findings.independence: Warrant terms and expiry from the FY2025 20-F (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001318885/000156276226000030/dsx-20251231.htm) and https://www.dianashippinginc.com/warrant-information. Same warrant terms as finding 2 but a different effect (supply, not P&L). The two do not conflict.

findings.finding: The Genco stake lost value after the quarter. GNK fell from $26.16 (Sep 30) to $23.23 (Nov 24), about -$12.1m on ~4.13m shares, partly offset by Genco's record $1.05 Q3 dividend (record Nov 16, about +$4.3m). Net is about -$7.8m (-$0.06 per share) for Q4 to date, against a single-source Q4 consensus of $0.21.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: GNK is a public quote and DSX has fallen alongside it. It could appear as a subsequent-events note or in the NAV discussion on the call.
findings.independence: GNK closes from the Yahoo chart (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/GNK). This is the same stake as finding 1 but a different period (Q4, not Q3), so it is not double-counted.

findings.finding: There is room for a capital-return change on Nov 25. The common dividend has been held at $0.01 for every quarter since Q1 2025 (Q2 2026: about $1.3m) while H1 2026 EPS was $0.41. The Genco bid is dead (withdrawn Aug 14). Diana raised about $57m from Genco share sales and about $29m from warrant exercises, and still holds about $96m of GNK. Management says DSX trades at a 'substantial discount to NAV', which is the usual setup for a buyback or a dividend restoration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend has not changed in 7 quarters, so there is no reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference from cash sources, not a company statement. A stock priced for a restoration would not sit 25% off its high. The size is small because nothing sourced says the board will act.
findings.independence: The withdrawal is documented at https://maritime-executive.com/article/diana-withdraws-offer-for-genco-as-sides-disagree-on-valuation and the stake sales at https://gcaptain.com/diana-shipping-cuts-genco-stake-below-10-weeks-after-abandoning-takeover-bid/. The step from those facts to a capital return is a proxy.

findings.finding: Q3 may carry write-offs of deal costs from the abandoned Genco bid. The tender offer was backed by $1.4bn of committed financing from six banks, and there were a proxy fight and a tender offer. It was withdrawn Aug 14, inside Q3. Q1/Q2 G&A ($8.3m in Q2 vs $8.9m a year earlier) shows no spike, so any capitalised advisory, legal or commitment fees would be expensed in Q3.
findings.why_not_priced: No filing quantifies these costs, so neither the bar nor I can size them. It is filed small because it is an inference with no number behind it.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/375049/) shows flat G&A and no transaction-cost line, which is consistent with deferral but does not prove it.

outside_window.finding: The DSX warrants expire Dec 14, 2026, which ends the effective $2.38 upside supply cap and any further exercise proceeds.

baseline_tension: The baseline is thin: no option anchor, no skew, no history. The evidence offsets: Q3 headline EPS probably lands near or modestly above a single $0.10 estimate, while the 25% slide from the September high reflects dilution and GNK weakness that the market already sees. Nothing cuts strongly against the -7.4% 20-day run-up.
lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs as fractions): Genco remeasurement gain cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and warrant remeasurement loss from -0.4 to -0.3. Both sit below operating income with no path to guidance.

Rule 5 / 'documents beat inference': the deal-cost write-off is pure inference with no number, so it was cut from -0.3 to -0.2. The warrant-arbitrage cap was cut from -0.5 to -0.4 because it is reasoning from terms, not an observed company number.
Rule 6 (bar from a single source): every finding was already capped small. Rule 8 does not apply, because no finding is a confirmed, unpriced, company-level number.
The sweep flagged the baseline history as untrustworthy, so reaction history was rebuilt from confirmed releases (-4.5, +4.4, -2.0, +7.5) and abs_move_pct set to 4.5.
Left standing: the TCE finding (+0.4), insider-exercise financing (+0.2, sign decided after asking what the money buys), the capital-return inference (+0.3) and the Q4-to-date Genco mark (-0.2).
